edge_explainer: The IBKR PEBB.TEN line is a HISTORICAL corporate action, not a live special situation: a GBP 6.5M fixed-price (not Dutch-auction) tender at 61p for 6.69% of the shares, launched 21-Jul-2025 and closed 07-Aug-2025, plus a successor GBP 7.0M open-market buyback launched 17-Mar-2026 and COMPLETED 30-Jul-2026 at an average 57.20p. Share count fell 159.4M -> 148.7M -> 136.5M in twelve months (-14.4%) and GBP 14.3M was returned in the 12m to 30-Jun-2026. The shelf's in_offer_period:false tag is technically correct but reveals a guard gap: an issuer self-tender is not a Takeover Code offer and can never appear in the Panel disclosure table, so self-tenders, buybacks and returns of capital need a separate detector keyed off IBKR .TEN/CORPACT lines and RNS headlines. Two adverse facts follow from the tender: US residents were expressly excluded from it, so a US taxable account is locked out of PEBB's premium return-of-capital channel; and the board's own marks (61p tender, 57.20p buyback VWAP) are both above today's 55.6p. On the business, the two-speed holdco runs the OPPOSITE way to the bull narrative. FY25 segment note: Brand Addition revenue GBP 107.502M, Adj EBITDA GBP 11.380M (10.6%), operating profit GBP 7.914M and RISING (GBP 6.2M FY23 -> 7.9M FY24 -> 7.914M FY25, gross margin 35.2% -> 37.0%). Facilisgroup revenue GBP 17.157M and FALLING for a third year (17.9 -> 17.6 -> 17.157), Adj EBITDA margin collapsing 60% -> 54% -> 50% -> 50% -> 42%, operating profit down ~43% in two years to GBP 2.431M, with GBP 4.5M/yr of development spend capitalised (GBP 3.474M of it staff costs) making the 42% EBITDA margin a capitalisation artifact. GMV grew to $1,580M but Preferred-Supplier spend went flat at $509M on US tariffs, so the take rate is compressing. The 'you get Facilisgroup for free' bull case is refuted by sum-of-the-parts: on EV of GBP 77.1M (corrected mcap GBP 75.88M + GBP 1.2M net debt at 30-Jun-26) less Brand Addition at a defensible 6-8x EBIT and adding back GBP 2.9M of central costs at 8x, the market is paying GBP 37-53M for Facilisgroup = 2.2-3.1x sales / 15-22x EBIT. Brand Addition cannot carry the 10x EBIT the bull case needs: top-10 clients are 61% of segment revenue and 53% of Group revenue, the largest is GBP 13.0M (12.1% of the segment), operating margin is 7.4% and GBP 15.4M of working capital is tied up. Screen battery: securities-as-cash NOT APPLICABLE; pension RESOLVED as defined-contribution only (GBP 853k cost, no DB scheme anywhere in the 2025 annual report, so no equity or EV adjustment); capital commitments CLEARED EXPLICITLY (note 26: 'no known commitments or contingencies', GBP 10.0M RCF undrawn to Feb-2029); share count FIRES and is corrected; trough-anchor shows EBIT at 0.74x the FY22 peak with 100% of the decline attributable to Facilisgroup; commodity frame not applicable; client-float check PARTIALLY FIRES — the FY25 year-end cash of GBP 9.637M carries GBP 4.790M of contract liabilities (subscriptions invoiced in advance) and 31-Dec is the seasonal peak, with the company reporting NET DEBT of GBP 1.2M at 30-Jun-2026 against net cash of GBP 6.0M a year earlier. The shelf's ncash_r of +5.4% is therefore stale, seasonally flattered and half customer money. The headline 19%-of-market-cap capital return was balance-sheet liquidation (net cash GBP 16.5M Dec-24 -> 9.6M Dec-25 -> ~5.0M guided Dec-26); the sustainable run-rate is post-tax free cash flow of ~GBP 6.3M = 8.3%. Fundamentals are 7 months stale (31-Dec-2025) and the intervening period changed the balance sheet materially. Verdict: an honestly-run, cash-generative business trading at roughly fair value (10.5x EV/EBIT, 4.9x EV/Adj EBITDA, 8.3% post-tax cash yield), near its high, with 6.1% of edge after friction, in a line whose only reliable bid retired on 30-Jul-2026. Reject on frame and on liquidity, not on quality.
